source_caption:
Quentin Tarantino originally envisioned the character of Jules Winnfield sporting a massive Afro as a visual tribute to 1970s Blaxploitation stars. However, a production assistant dispatched to purchase the hairpiece mistakenly returned with a Jheri curl wig instead. When Samuel L. Jackson tried it on during a makeup test, he immediately embraced the error, arguing to Tarantino that the slick, heavily maintained hairstyle perfectly aligned with the meticulous, calculating nature of a professional hitman. The director agreed to the on-the-fly pivot, turning an accidental wardrobe flub into one of the most recognizable character silhouettes of 1990s cinema.

Pulp Fiction (1994), directed by Quentin Tarantino, starring John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Uma Thurman, Bruce Willis. The lives of two philosophical mob hitmen, a desperate aging boxer, a ruthless gangster and his unpredictable wife, and a pair of frantic diner bandits violently intertwine in a groundbreaking, non-linear narrative exploring the seedy underbelly of Los Angeles.

source_details.title: Pulp Fiction
source_details.synopsis: Pulp Fiction is a 1994 American crime film written and directed by Quentin Tarantino from a story he conceived with Roger Avary. It tells four intertwining tales of crime and violence in Los Angeles. The film stars John Travolta, Samuel L. Jackson, Bruce Willis, Tim Roth, Ving Rhames, and Uma Thurman. The title refers to the pulp magazines and hardboiled crime novels popular during the mid-twentieth century, known for their graphic violence and punchy dialogue. Tarantino wrote Pulp Fiction in 1992 and 1993, incorporating scenes that Avary originally wrote for True Romance (1993). Its plot occurs out of chronological order.
